h1: Charlie's Bungalows — Garden Bungalows on Ko Si Chang Near Thewawong Pier
intro: Ko Si Chang is a small island off Si Racha that Bangkokians love to escape to for the weekend, because it's only about a 45-minute boat ride from Chuk Samet Pier and you get a quiet island feel that isn't as crowded as the sea on other coasts — Charlie's Bungalows is one of the most talked-about places to stay on the island · it's 14 detached bungalows set in a green garden, run by the owners and their family, each with AC, hot water, a fridge, a TV and a private balcony looking over the garden · it sits in the middle of the island within walking distance of restaurants and the market, near Thewawong Pier and Phra Chudadhuj Palace · there's motorbike rental and pier pickup that make it easy to ride around the island · from about ฿930/night · around 9.0 from real reviews across several platforms.

body.html: When Bangkokians want a quick hit of the sea without driving all the way out east or down south, Ko Si Chang is usually one of the first names that comes to mind, because you just drive to Si Racha, catch the boat at Chuk Samet Pier and after about 45 minutes you're on an island that's still quiet and very natural · on this little island Charlie's Bungalows is one of the most talked-about places to stay · it isn't a fancy beachfront resort and it isn't a budget hostel in a shophouse — it's 14 detached bungalows in a tropical garden, run by the owners and their family, sitting in the middle of the island in Tha Thewawong sub-district · this review is put together from the voices of real guest reviews across several platforms — Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com and Tripadvisor — rather than a stay of our own, so you can see both the good points and the honest caveats before you decide to book.

The big picture and who it suits — if we had to sum it up in one line, Charlie's Bungalows is for people who want to come to Ko Si Chang for something "simple but clean and reassuring" rather than those chasing luxury or every last amenity · the main draw is getting a private detached bungalow of your own, with no shared walls or walkways, set among a shady, peaceful green garden · so the people it suits best are couples after a quiet break, solo travellers who want to ride a motorbike around the island, and small families travelling in a small group · plenty of reviews agree that the charm here is the feeling of staying at a kind relative's house — the owners recognise your face, greet you warmly and help with everything from picking you up at the pier to recommending restaurants · on the other hand, if you expect a hotel where you step out of your room straight onto the sand, with a pool and an in-house restaurant, or you want a sleek, luxurious modern room, this place may not match what you're hoping for, because it's a garden bungalow in the middle of the island that's about quiet, cleanliness and family-style care rather than grandeur.

Location and getting there — Charlie's Bungalows sits at 39/2 Moo 2, Tha Thewawong sub-district, in the middle of Ko Si Chang, a community zone with restaurants, convenience stores and a market all within walking distance · the upside of this location is that food and supplies are easy — no need to ride far when you're hungry or want to buy something · getting to the island starts by driving or taking a car to Chuk Samet Pier in Si Racha district, then catching the passenger ferry across, which takes about 45 minutes to reach Thewawong Pier on the island, after which the property isn't far from the pier · something many people like is that the property offers pier transfers when you let them know in advance, so you don't have to drag your bags on foot or haggle with a songthaew yourself · for getting around the island, a highlight here is that motorbikes are available to rent for around 300 baht a day with a full tank of fuel, which is the most convenient way to see Ko Si Chang since the island has its ups and downs and the sights are scattered across several corners · Phra Chudadhuj Palace (the old summer palace) is close by, a few minutes on foot or by motorbike · one thing reviews consistently mention is that the property isn't on the beach — popular beaches like Tham Phang Beach and Laem Phrom Thep are on the other side of the island, so you'll need to ride a motorbike or take a skylab cart, about 5–10 minutes.

"Just a forty-five-minute boat ride from Si Racha, and the owner picked us up right at the pier. We rented a motorbike and rode around the island all day. The room was small but really clean, the garden was shady, and we slept well in the quiet — like staying at a kind relative's house."

Room types and decor — the heart of this place is the detached garden bungalow, not a room in a block · there are 14 bungalows in all, split into several types by group size and bed type · they start with Twin and Double bungalows for couples or two people, and go up to larger ones that take more guests for small families · every one is an air-conditioned bungalow with a hot-water heater, fridge, flat-screen TV, a kettle with tea and coffee sachets, and free Wi-Fi · what reviews praise most consistently is that the rooms are very clean, the linens and towels are clean, and the build feels solid and new — many say the bungalows are compact but have everything you need · every one has a private balcony with chairs to sip a coffee and look over the garden morning or evening, a detail that makes it feel relaxing · the decor is a warm-toned garden-bungalow style that leans on cleanliness and practicality rather than flashy design · a caveat that comes up often in reviews is that the mattresses are fairly firm in the Thai style — some people who like a soft mattress may not be used to it, and a few bungalows have a bit too little shelving or luggage space, so it's best to set your expectations at "a clean, comfortable bungalow at a good price" rather than "a luxury resort room with everything."

Amenities and the garden setting — Charlie's Bungalows doesn't have a pool or a gym like a big resort, but what earns it praise is its shady tropical garden and neatly kept gravel paths · many reviews describe it as a small, peaceful oasis in the middle of the island, lovely for a stroll in the garden in the evening · the grounds have a barbecue area for anyone who wants to buy seafood and grill it themselves, plus free parking, CCTV in the common areas, laundry service and a staffed reception counter · the service highlight is the motorbike rental and pier transfers, which matter a lot on an island where the sights are scattered and there's no city-style public transport · free Wi-Fi covers the common areas · worth knowing: the amenities here lean toward being a simple island stay — there's no in-house restaurant, no pool and no breakfast service, so if you want all of that in one place you may need to look at a bigger resort, but for people who plan to spend their time out on the island and just use the room to sleep, this simplicity is actually a plus.

Food and dining — because the property has no in-house restaurant and no breakfast, the dining style for guests here is to head out to find places in the island town, which the central community location helps a lot with, since a few minutes' walk gets you to made-to-order eateries, coffee shops, convenience stores and a small market · Ko Si Chang is known for fresh, inexpensive seafood, and many people walk over to eat seafood by the sea or at a market eatery in the evening · for those who want to cook for themselves, the property has a barbecue area to use — buy fresh seafood and grill it in the garden — and the room has a fridge plus a kettle with tea and coffee sachets · some reviews suggest bringing along some drinking water and snacks, because a few places on the island close early at night · overall, the food situation here is "small-island flexibility" — no fancy resort buffet, but step out and you'll find tasty local food at friendly prices, which fits the charm of a Ko Si Chang trip nicely.

Service — this is the point that earns the most praise in the real reviews of Charlie's Bungalows · because it's a property run by the owners and their family, many people feel a level of care you don't find at a big hotel · a lot of reviews describe the owners and team as friendly, kind and helpful with everything — from picking you up at the pier and sorting out a motorbike rental to recommending restaurants and sights, right down to handling the small things during your stay · a phrase that comes up often in reviews is the feeling of being "a real guest, not just a customer," and many say it's the main reason they want to come back · a caveat found in some reviews is that contacting them in advance by email or the old website can be slow to get a reply — it's better to book through a booking platform or contact them by phone/page · another thing is that at times the property only takes cash, not credit cards, so bring enough cash · overall, service is the strongest point and the heart of why the review scores are high.

Voices from real reviews (praise and gripes) — pulling it together from several platforms, the picture is fairly consistent and the scores are high, with Trip.com at around 9.7 from 44 reviews and Tripadvisor around 4.4 out of 5 · On the praise side: the owners and family are friendly and very helpful, the detached bungalows are clean and private, the garden is shady and quiet like an oasis, the central location is within walking distance of restaurants and the market, the motorbike rental is good value with a full tank, the pier transfers are convenient, and it's good value for money · On the caveat side: the most talked-about thing is that the property isn't on the beach and you have to ride a motorbike or take a cart to the beach on the other side of the island, and that the mattresses are fairly firm in the Thai style · after that come too little shelving in the room, no restaurant or breakfast at the property, slow replies to email via the old website, and cash-only at certain times · most of these gripes are things you can manage by preparing ahead and setting your expectations to a simple island bungalow, rather than big problems that stop people coming back.

"Lovely bungalow, clean, and the owner was so kind. The only downsides are that it's not on the beach — you have to ride a motorbike to the other side — and the mattress was a touch firm. But for the price and the quiet garden setting it was great value. We'll be back next time."

Price and value — bungalows start at about ฿930/night at the regular rate, rising to around ฿1,200–1,500 for the larger ones or during long holidays and the tourist season · compared with other places on Ko Si Chang, which range from cheap guesthouses to pricey beachfront resorts, Charlie's Bungalows sits in the mid-range group that offers clear value, because you get a private detached bungalow that's clean, with AC and hot water all in, plus attentive owner service, at a price that isn't expensive · what makes it especially good value are the extras like motorbike rental and pier transfers, which save both money and hassle when getting around the island · if you're planning to come to Ko Si Chang to ride around, take in the views and relax quietly rather than lounge in a luxury resort, every baht you spend here pays off · on the other hand, if your heart is set on a beachfront room with a pool, the value drops because that isn't what this place offers.

Things to know before you book — there are several things that make the stay smoother · one, let them know your arrival time at the pier in advance so you can use the transfer and not have to haggle for a ride yourself · two, if you plan to ride around the island, book a motorbike rental ahead, especially during long holidays when they can all get rented out · three, bring enough cash, because at times the property and shops on the island only take cash · four, if you like a soft mattress, know that the mattresses here are fairly firm in the Thai style, and you can ask for extra pillows or bedding · five, the property isn't on the beach, so if you mainly plan to swim in the sea, allow for the trip to Tham Phang Beach or Laem Phrom Thep on the other side of the island · six, check the ferry schedule from Chuk Samet Pier carefully, since the boats run in rounds and the last one isn't late · seven, during long holidays Ko Si Chang gets crowded and bungalows fill up fast, so book ahead · for booking direct or asking for details, you can reach them through a booking platform or the property's own channels, alongside booking via Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com.

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Charlie's Bungalows is the best fit for people who want to come to Ko Si Chang for something simple and quiet, with owners who look after you like family · the strengths are detached bungalows that are clean and private, a shady, quiet garden, a central island location within walking distance of restaurants and the market, motorbike rental and pier transfers that make getting around easy, and clear value for money · the trade-off you have to accept is that it's a simple bungalow, not a luxury resort — not on the beach, no pool or in-house restaurant, fairly firm mattresses, and cash-only at certain times · if you're looking for a beachfront room with a pool and the full service of a big resort, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a beachfront resort on the island instead · but if your goal is a clean bungalow in a quiet garden, riding a motorbike around the island, and warm care at a price you can manage — Charlie's Bungalows is the right fit for that kind of Ko Si Chang trip, and it's why it has kept earning high review scores.

honestSummary: Charlie's Bungalows is a garden bungalow in the middle of Ko Si Chang that suits people who want a quiet, simple getaway with owners who look after you like family — clean, private detached bungalows, a shady garden, motorbike rental and pier transfers, and good value · but you have to accept that it's a simple place, not on the beach, with no pool or in-house restaurant, fairly firm mattresses, and cash-only at certain times.
honestChecks: If you're mainly here to swim in the sea — the property is in the middle of the island, not on the beach, so you'll need to ride a motorbike or take a cart to Tham Phang Beach / Laem Phrom Thep on the other side → allow for the trip and rent a motorbike.

If you like a soft mattress and a luxury resort-style room — the mattresses here are fairly firm in the Thai style and it's a simple bungalow → set your expectations on cleanliness and privacy, or ask for extra bedding/pillows.
If you plan to pay by card — at times the property and shops on the island only take cash → bring enough cash before you board the boat.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Charlie's Bungalows, Ko Si Chang

faq.q: Where is Charlie's Bungalows and how do you get there?
faq.a: It's at 39/2 Moo 2, Tha Thewawong sub-district, central Ko Si Chang, Ko Si Chang district, Chonburi province · getting there starts by driving to Chuk Samet Pier in Si Racha, then taking the ferry across, about 45 minutes to Thewawong Pier · the property is near the pier and offers transfers when you let them know in advance · it's within walking distance of restaurants and the market in the island town.

faq.q: Is Charlie's Bungalows on the beach?
faq.a: No, it isn't on the beach · the property is in the middle of the island in the community zone · popular beaches like Tham Phang Beach and Laem Phrom Thep are on the other side of the island, about 5–10 minutes by motorbike or car · the upside is being near restaurants and the pier, while anyone mainly here to swim should rent a motorbike.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Charlie's Bungalows and what are the rooms like?
faq.a: Prices start at about ฿930/night for a twin-bed bungalow · there are double-bed bungalows and larger ones for small families, with prices moving up to around ฿1,200–1,500 by size and season · every one is a detached bungalow with AC, hot water, a fridge, a TV and a private balcony · prices rise during long holidays, so compare several platforms before you book.

faq.q: Does Charlie's Bungalows have motorbikes for rent?
faq.a: Yes · the property rents motorbikes at around 300 baht a day with a full tank, which is the most convenient way to see Ko Si Chang since the sights are scattered and the island has its ups and downs · during long holidays they can all get rented out, so it's best to book ahead.

faq.q: Who does Charlie's Bungalows suit best?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, solo travellers and small families who want a quiet, simple Ko Si Chang getaway · you get a clean detached bungalow in a shady garden, owners who look after you like family, and motorbikes for rent to explore the island · it's not really for people who want a beachfront room with a pool and the full service of a big resort.

faq.q: How can you book Charlie's Bungalows, and do they take credit cards?
faq.a: You can book through Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com, or contact the property directly · worth knowing: at times the property and shops on the island only take cash, not credit cards, so bring enough cash before you board the boat, as ATMs on the island are limited.
